record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the Beverton-Holt periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = K mu x_n/(K + (mu - 1)x_n) - h_n with K > 0, mu > 1, and a p-periodic sequence h_n of nonnegative harvesting quotas that gives a nonempty persistent set, compare the average of the attracting population cycle for one ordering of the quotas with the average for any permutation of the same quotas. How does xbar_av, the attractor average for h_n, relate to xhat_av, the attractor average for the permuted sequence hhat_n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix constants $K>0$ and $\mu>1$, and let $p\ge 2$ be an integer. Consider the periodically harvested Beverton–Holt difference equation
$$x_{n+1} \;=\; \frac{K\mu\, x_n}{K+(\mu-1)x_n} \;-\; h_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
where $\{h_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative harvesting quotas. Assume the quotas $(h_0,h_1,\dots,h_{p-1})$ are chosen so that the equation admits a nonempty persistent set (i.e., there exist initial conditions for which $x_n>0$ for all $n$) and a globally attracting $p$-periodic cycle $(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_{p-1})$ on this set. Define the attractor average
$$\bar x_{\mathrm{av}} \;=\; \frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\bar x_n.$$
Let $\sigma$ be any permutation of $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$, and set $\hat h_n = h_{\sigma(n)}$ extended $p$-periodically. Assume the permuted equation
$$y_{n+1}=\frac{K\mu\, y_n}{K+(\mu-1)y_n}-\hat h_n$$
also has a nonempty persistent set with globally attracting cycle $(\hat x_0,\dots,\hat x_{p-1})$, and let $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\hat x_n$. Determine the precise relationship between $\bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$ and $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$: characterize those permutations $\sigma$ for which $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}=\bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$, and for the remaining permutations decide whether $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}\le \bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$ or $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}\ge \bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$, or otherwise describe how the attractor average changes under permutation of the harvesting quotas.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (AlSharawi et al., "The effect of maps permutation on the global attractor of a periodic Beverton–Holt model," Applied Mathematics and Computation, 2020) addresses this problem. The authors show that the total harvesting yield is invariant under permutation, that all permutations within the dihedral group (rotations and reflections of the cyclic ordering) yield the same attractor average, and obtain a characterization based on block reflections of the harvesting quotas describing when other permutations change the attractor average. The problem is therefore partially resolved, though a complete comparison for arbitrary permutations is not fully closed.

status_evidence.title: The effect of maps permutation on the global attractor of a periodic Beverton–Holt model
status_evidence.snippet: Members of the dihedral group give the same population geometric-mean... block reflection of the harvesting quotas is investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Permutations within the dihedral group preserve the attractor average; a characterization via block reflections describes other permutations.
